subject: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples
body:
From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@legalik.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@legalik.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Model fit recap: from the demo and the use cases you described (contract review triage + clause extraction + first-pass redlines), our initial read is that a medium-sized open model fine-tuned for legal Q&A will give the best balance of latency and cost. Specific candidates: Redwood-optimized 13B quantized variant for high-concurrency endpoints, and a 70B Llama-derivative for high-quality batch jobs (longer context).

- Benchmarks & evals: I uploaded a short evaluation plan and benchmark folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF-eval-roadmap — it includes the token cost estimates, latency profiles, and recommended metrics (exact-match for extraction tasks, F1 for clause detection, and a small quality rubric for redlining suggestions).

- We need your help: to run a targeted eval we need a representative prompt set (both happy-path and edge cases). Can you share ~30–50 de-identified prompts/examples that cover: typical contract snippets, ambiguous clauses, short Q&A about obligations, and two examples of intentionally messy OCR input? We attached a CSV template (sample_prompt_set.csv) — please drop examples into the “prompt_example” column.

- Redaction: you asked about PII handling — attached is a short note on redaction guidance we typically provide (redaction_guidelines_brief.pdf). If you have stricter requirements (e.g., SID/SSN/financial account numbers never leave the customer environment), we can route your eval to a private deployment or use client-side redaction before sending prompts. Please indicate which redaction policy you prefer.

- Timeline & next steps we propose:
  1) You share the prompt CSV + a pointer to any internal evaluation criteria by EOD next Wednesday (2026-09-09).
  2) We run an automated pass (sanity checks + initial metric sweep) and deliver a short model recommendation and cost estimate within 5 business days of receiving prompts.
  3) Joint review call to agree on canary tests and SLA needs.

Attachments: sample_prompt_set.csv (template), redaction_guidelines_brief.pdf (stub)

Let me know if that timeline works. If it does, I’ll preview the eval plan with Ben and schedule initial work.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@legalik.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@legalik.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples

Thanks, Priyom — great demo. A few quick notes: 

1) We can assemble the prompt set but need to confirm redaction constraints. Legalik is not comfortable with raw SSNs or bank account numbers leaving our VPC. We can provide de-identified prompts but would like a guarantee that any sample prompt containing sensitive tokens will be redacted client-side. Is that supported for the hosted eval?

2) We have a mix of clean digital docs and scanned PDFs — the OCR mess examples are important. I’ll put 10 clean + 10 edge + 5 OCR examples in the CSV and share them with you by Tue 9/8 COB.

3) Quick question on metrics: can you include examples of the rubric you mentioned? We want to see how you score redline suggestions — precision on flagged clauses matters to our legal ops team.

–Elena
Director of Product, Legalik

---

On Fri, 4 Sep 2026 at 11:05, ben_carter@redwood.example.com wrote:
From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, Elena Ruiz <elena@legalik.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples

Hi all — quick technical addendum to Priyom’s note: 

- Model recommendations: we’ll initially test two variants: Redwood-13B-q (quantized, lower cost, good for interactive throughput) and Llama70B-v2-cand (higher quality for batch processing). We’ll also run a lightweight safety check against hallucination-prone outputs for redline suggestions.

- Rubric preview: here are the metrics we’ll report back in the first sweep — Exact Match (for extraction), F1/Precision/Recall (for clause detection), and a subjective quality score (0–5) for redline helpfulness along with a short justification. I’ve put an example rubric in the Drive folder link Priyom shared.

- Data handling note: for hosted evals we recommend client-side redaction for anything legally sensitive. If Legalik prefers, we can perform the eval on Redwood Private (VPC) to keep raw prompts inside your network; that will add setup time but is straightforward.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for how we handle OCR/noisy text and share it with the team before the initial sweep.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, Elena Ruiz <elena@legalik.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples

Hi Elena —

One quick procurement note: Legal typically asks for a one-page SOW for the eval (scope, acceptance criteria, timeline). I can draft that as soon as we confirm the prompt set and redaction approach. Also happy to take the first pass on contract redlines — if you want to send over your template we’ll avoid surprises.

Attached: redlines_contract_v1.pdf (stub)

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability, eval roadmap, and request for customer prompt samples

Elena — that timeline works. Appreciate the redaction constraint callout; client-side redaction is fine for the hosted eval or we can spin up a short Private eval if you prefer.

Next actions I’ll take:
- Confirm with Ben we’ll prioritize Redwood-13B-q for the interactive tranche and Llama70B for batch.
- Marissa will draft a one-page SOW and initial redlines; Marissa, can you share a draft by Wed 9/9?
- Elena/Tom: please drop the CSV by Tue 9/8 COB as discussed.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute check-in for Friday 9/11 to go over initial results and rubric. Calendar invite coming.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
